summary:
COMBAT is built and replaces the stub: hit-target registry and traces, the one damage entry point, per-target hit-confirm feedback, pooled projectiles with continuous collision, the FIFO explosion queue with its full audiovisual package, and instanced projectile meshes. It is verified by 141 unit tests and in the running game on port 5212; smoke passes 48/48 and the god-mode campaign reaches victory with no errors.

Two limits on that verification. Render and audio are still stubs, so glow brightness was judged only through an emulated tone curve and no sound was heard. Enemy kinds are placeholders, so enemy projectiles were only fired by my check scripts.

What exists, by module in `/home/user/Testing-2/src/combat/`:
- **`targets.ts`** — registry in registration order, nearest hit, nearest enabled sphere per target, piercing trace (near to far, each target once, overflow keeps the nearest), thick rays for targets only, radius query, faction and `ignoreId` filtering.
- **`feedback.ts`** — one spark per damaging ray at once; one damage number, one 2D hit sound (kill > crit > shield > armour > plain) and one `'hit:confirmed'` per target per substep, flushed from `update`.
- **`explosions.ts`** — always queued, resolved FIFO in `update` including chains, 32 per update. Falloff to the bounding sphere, cover test, faction / self-damage / friendly-fire / exclude / credit rules, and the package: recipe sized to the radius, scorch, sound (distant beyond 40 m), light, shake, rumble within 12 m, and close-range chromatic boost, screen flash and hit-stop.
- **`projectiles.ts`** — pool of 96 (oldest makes room silently), each on its own clock, swept against world and hostile targets, bounce / roll / rest, fuses, lifetime, bounds, homing, landing telegraph, shoot-down, whiz-by, mortar whistle, fly loops, trails, world impacts, per-projectile error containment.
- **`visuals.ts`** — four instanced body meshes on one lit material plus one additive glow mesh for everything that glows; at most 5 draw calls, none while nothing flies.
- **`tuning.ts`** holds every combat-internal number; **`testkit.ts`** is test support only.

Traces and a substep with 90 projectiles in flight allocate nothing, measured with the physics heap meter. In `src/data/projectiles.ts` I lowered three collision radii (plasmaBolt 0.2 → 0.16, lightBolt 0.12 → 0.1, bossBolt 0.3 → 0.26) so enemy bolts are drawn larger than they hit.

gates.typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E "^src/combat/"` prints nothing. The whole project also type-checked with 0 errors when I last ran it unfiltered, with the fx engineer's in-progress files present. `--noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters` is clean for src/combat.
gates.unitTests: `npx vitest run src/combat`: 6 files, 141 of 141 pass (targets 20, damage 21, explosions 33, projectiles 57, system 7, alloc 3). The whole repo ran 372 of 372 in 12 files on my second-to-last code state. The alloc suite passed 4 consecutive runs and once inside the parallel full suite.
gates.smoke: `node tools/smoke.mjs --mode dev --port 5212`: ok, 48 of 48 checks, exit 0, on the final code. `node tools/campaign.mjs --mode dev --port 5212 --god 1`: ok, victory after 526 simulated seconds, 0 errors, 0 NaN frames, 0 assists.
gates.liveCheck:
Driven through tools/harness.mjs on port 5212 at 960x540, with the stub render / player / weapons / enemies and the fx engineer's in-progress fx. Scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Testing-2/6bb73113-d5ad-55b7-9619-608c6eaa77e8/scratchpad/combat.

Measured:
- Vector on a riveter: 5 hits of 14, at most one 'hit:confirmed' per target per substep, stats.damageDealt 70.
- Breaker on a bulwark: nine pellets gave exactly one event of 99.
- Hornet: direct hit killed target A (90 dealt, excluded from the splash), neighbour B took 62.4 splash; one event each; no self-damage at 20 m.
- Overclock: in 0.5 s a player rocket at 20 m/s moved 10.0 m and an enemy bolt at 20 m/s moved 4.0 m (scale 0.4).
- explode(): nothing changes inside the call; after the next update chromaticBoost was 0.286, flash 0.124, hitstop scale 0.05.
- Boss missile shot down with the rifle: explosionSmall at radius 1.4, 'hitKill', player vitals unchanged at 200.
- Rocket fired with the nose against a wall: burst on the near face, 31.5 self-damage (90 x 0.35).
- Mortar lobbed at the player: 'mortar' telegraph at the player, radius 4.5, 1.4 s, owner = projectile id; whistle with owner; direct hit of 35 and no double dip.
- Restart: 0 projectiles, 0 visible combat meshes.
- Shader programs stayed at 20 before and after the first projectiles were drawn.
- Budget: 5 visible meshes with all seven kinds on screen; 3 meshes and 44k triangles with 96 projectiles.
- Cost: combat.update 0.039 ms with 96 projectiles and 40 enemies; traceShot about 1 microsecond.
- Glow shader compiled and rendered without errors under both FogExp2 and Fog.

Looked at (Read tool):
- Lineups of all seven kinds from the side, head-on, three-quarter and close, iterated four times. Glows went from blown-out white blobs to thin accent collars, engine streaks and comet bolts.
- First-person sequences of incoming volleys and outgoing rocket and grenade, with and without fx. Trails start at the muzzle and converge on the aim line.
- Blast packages for all five looks. A ground blast now shows a single ring; a burst 3 m up shows the recipe's ring in the air plus mine on the floor.
- Hit sparks and merged numbers by part on four enemies: 27 body, 54 crit, 14 armour, shield hexes with no number.

contractRequests: ProjectileOptions.knockback has no doc: direct-hit impulse, blast impulse, or both? I use it for both: direct hit = the value or 0, blast = the value or the explosion default of 6.

FxSpawnOptions.dir is documented as 'main emission direction', but the fx recipes for hitEnemy* treat it as the shot's travel direction and reverse it. I pass normal = out of the struck sphere and dir = info.dir. The contract should state this convention for hit sparks.

'shockwaveRing' is listed as spawned by combat.explode, but not when. The fx explosion recipes already draw their own ring. I spawn it only under an air burst 0.4 to 0.75 radii above the floor, with radius = the damage radius.

CombatSystem offers no read access to a projectile (position, velocity, kind); only projectileCount. Shootable ones are reachable through getTarget(id).center. AI or UI that wants to warn about an incoming rocket or mortar has no API. My tests read the trail's retained vector.

The DamageResult of a shot-down projectile is unspecified. I return dealt = info.amount and killed = true, so the player gets a number, 'hitKill' and 'hit:confirmed'. Consequences: stats.damageDealt includes it, and hit:confirmed.targetId can be a projectile id.

The contract says the hit spark is chosen by result.part. For a hit that was fully absorbed on a non-shield part (an invulnerable boss), that gives a body spark with a shield sound. I use the shield spark whenever result.absorbed is true. Please confirm or rule.

Unspecified details I had to choose: decal kind and size per ExplosionVisual; the 'listener' for the 40 m distant-sound rule (I use ctx.camera.position); whether ProjectileDef.radius also applies to the world for bouncing shells (I use it, so a grenade rests on its radius).

ExplosionOptions cannot carry the surface a blast sits on (normal, boxId). For external callers combat probes for the nearest surface (down first, then five axes) to place the scorch and orient the recipe.
judgementCalls: applyDamage deals 0 to a HitTarget object that is not the registered entry of its id, and to a NaN amount. Hit feedback is recorded only when info.amount > 0.
A merged damage number below 0.5 is not drawn (no floating '0' for an absorbed hit); the sound and the event still go out.
With several targets flushed in one substep, hit sounds play at volume n^-0.75 each; kills never below 0.6.

Explosion cover test uses three rays: blast to centre, lifted origin to centre, lifted origin to a head sample at centre + 0.6 boundRadius. The origin is lifted 0.5 m (headroom permitting) so a kerb next to a shell on the floor is not cover. A wall still blocks.
A blast with damage 0 and knockback 0 is presentation only; victims whose share is 0 are not called at all.
Chained blasts resolve damage and fx immediately, but their sounds are staggered 35 ms each with slightly falling volume. The distant variant is delayed by distance / 343, capped at 0.6 s.

Close-range treatment scales to 0 at radius * 1.2 + 3 m from the camera. The screen flash needs line of sight. Hit-stop and rumble only while playing with a live player. Only large, shock and boss looks hit-stop (0.04 to 0.07 s).
Blast light is a warm fire colour (0xffa45a) that is none of the five accents; plasma takes the faction or projectile accent, boss takes elite magenta.
A bouncing or resting shell detonates on contact with a hostile target. If its direct damage is 0 (a grenade), the struck target is not excluded from the splash, since there is nothing to double.

Bounce model: tangential speed keeps 72 % per bounce; a floor rebound under 1.3 m/s switches to rolling (8 m/s^2 deceleration), then rest below 0.35 m/s. A resting shell checks for hostile contact every step.
Fuse and lifetime end the step exactly at their time; flight is the exact parabola per step flown as a chord, so impacts are frame-rate independent.

Launch guard: if the world lies between the shooter's axis (at muzzle height) and the launch point, the shell is put back 2 cm in front of that wall. This stops rockets passing through a wall the shooter is hugging; firing over low cover still works.
A shootable projectile never collides with its own hit target, whatever its faction. Its hit sphere is 1.5 times its collision radius.
A shot-down projectile goes off through the normal queue as a 'small' blast of radius 1.4 with no damage and no push, because explosion* effects may only come from combat.explode.
bulletWhiz plays once per enemy projectile, non-bouncing and at least 10 m/s, at its closest point to the eye when that pass happens within 2 m.
mortarWhistle plays once when a 'mortar' starts to fall, owner-bound. A fly loop that audio could not give at launch is retried every 0.5 s.
One keyed travelling light, on the newest live player rocket only, leaving the second keyed slot to other systems.

Landing telegraph: predicted with 1/30 s chords; dropped to the floor below when the shell would strike a wall; none when it leaves the world. A player-clock shell gets a persistent marker driven by setProgress.
Bounds removal margins: 4 m sideways, 6 m below, 80 m above world.bounds.

Invalid explode / spawnProjectile requests (non-finite numbers, unknown kind) are ignored and reported at most 3 times each under 'combat:explode' / 'combat:spawnProjectile', so a caller bug is visible but never fatal. spawnProjectile returns 0.

The trace broad phase uses max(boundRadius, measured reach of the spheres), refreshed once per update, so a weak point outside a too-small boundRadius stays hittable. Explosions and queryRadius use boundRadius as the contract says.

A thick-ray hit reports its point on the real sphere surface (distance stays the along-ray distance). Equal distances resolve to the first sphere listed, then the first target registered; a target at exactly the world distance wins over the world.
Projectile looks: solid ordnance is lit vertex-coloured geometry; every accent is a glow volume (thin collar discs, engine streaks, comet bolts). Bolts are drawn larger than their collision radius.

Hot-path code exchanges numbers through Float64Array scratch, uses integer ray lengths, and spells 'never' as a numeric literal. V8 boxes fractional arguments of non-inlined calls and fractions merged with `Infinity`; this is what makes the zero-allocation tests pass.
integrationNotes: Render is a stub (no HDR target, bloom or tone map). The glow shader outputs linear colour without tonemapping / colorspace chunks, as the contract demands; I judged it through a filmic curve patched in by my harness script only. Final brightness must be re-judged once render lands: the gains are the GlowSpec table and `hot` factor in src/combat/visuals.ts.
Audio is a stub: no sound was heard. Verified only that the right ids are called with the right owner, position, volume and delay (unit tests plus a live call log).
Enemy kinds are placeholders: plasma / light / boss bolts, mortars and missiles were fired only by my scripts. Tick chains were tested in vitest with fake targets.
Enemy kinds must pass ownerId = actor.id: it is what keeps a shell from hitting its shooter and feeds the launch guard. Enemy projectiles home on the player by default only when homing > 0.

The boss kind can follow its missiles through ctx.combat.getTarget(id).center while they live. 'hit:confirmed' for a shot-down missile carries the projectile id as targetId, so listeners that look it up as an enemy must tolerate undefined.

Weapons: a grenade launched with damage 0 gives a struck enemy its full splash; with damage > 0 the struck target takes only the direct hit. `knockback` on ProjectileOptions drives both direct hit and blast.

FX conventions I matched from src/fx as it stands: hitEnemy* get dir = shot travel direction; decal size is a diameter; explosion recipes draw their own ring and ground themselves within 0.4 radii; trail default colours equal my accent mapping, and I pass the accent explicitly.
My BLAST_FEEL.ringMinHeight (0.4) mirrors the fx recipes' grounding reach. If fx changes that constant, ground rings may double or go missing for blasts between the two values.
Player and render stubs accept addShakeAt, screenFlash and post.chromaticBoost but do nothing visible; those three were verified as calls and values only.
For zero-allocation traces, callers should keep one TraceOptions object shape per call site. With more than four shapes V8 boxes a fractional `radius` on load; that is outside combat's control.
src/data/projectiles.ts: plasmaBolt, lightBolt and bossBolt collision radii were lowered (0.16 / 0.1 / 0.26). Anything that reads these for lead or spacing sees the new values.
The orchestrator snapshot-committed part of my directory mid-work (commit 1f4b2be). I ran no state-changing git command.
openIssues: Looks under the real HDR + bloom + tone-map pipeline are unverified; only the emulated curve on the stub renderer was seen.
Geometry buffers of the five projectile meshes are uploaded on first draw (geometries 39 to 44 in the live check), not in init. Shader programs are warmed; the upload is a few kilobytes.
The logarithmic-depth chunks of the glow shader are included but untested; the stub renderer has no such mode.

A bouncing shell treats a struck surface as an infinite plane one radius early, so near box edges contact can be a few centimetres early. Leftover time after 4 contacts in one step, or after settling into a roll, is dropped.
A projectile moving parallel to a wall closer than its radius overlaps it visually; non-bouncing projectiles are points against the world.
Hit-stop, shake and rumble strengths, the bounce feel and the glow sizes are first-pass tuning against stubs; they need a play-feel pass once player, weapons and render are real.
The one explicit reset-during-flush case is tested for the feedback flush only. A reset from inside a victim's takeDamage during a blast is handled by code (victim list cleared) but has no test.
